name: Hemiconvulsion-Hemiplegia-Epilepsy Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for Hemiconvulsion-Hemiplegia-Epilepsy Syndrome

criteria.description: Prolonged unilateral convulsive seizure (hemiconvulsion) typically in infancy or early childhood
Development of persistent hemiplegia ipsilateral to the convulsive side following the hemiconvulsion
Subsequent development of chronic focal epilepsy involving the affected hemisphere
Neuroimaging evidence of unilateral cerebral hemiatrophy or gliosis corresponding to clinical hemiplegia
Exclusion of other causes of hemiplegia and epilepsy such as stroke, infection, or metabolic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prolonged unilateral convulsive seizure followed by persistent hemiplegia and subsequent chronic focal epilepsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by neuroimaging and exclusion of other etiologies.

searchTerms: extended convulsion affecting one body side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent hemiplegia ipsilateral to seizure side
Chronic focal epilepsy involving affected hemisphere
searchTerms: chronic seizures in one brain hemisphere
limping or abnormal walking due to weakness
loss of half visual field opposite brain lesion
blindness in one half of vision
hemianopia affecting one side of sight

rare.symptomName: Hemiatrophy of affected side of body
searchTerms: wasting of one side of body

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; exclusion of metabolic or infectious causes
imaging: MRI showing unilateral cerebral hemiatrophy, gliosis, or cortical laminar necrosis
CT scan may show cerebral atrophy ipsilateral to hemiplegia
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; mostly sporadic cases
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing focal epileptiform discharges in affected hemisphere

distinguishingFeatures: Sudden onset hemiplegia without preceding prolonged hemiconvulsion
Imaging shows vascular infarction rather than hemiatrophy
Progressive neurological decline with unilateral inflammation
Presence of chronic encephalitis on biopsy

redFlags: Prolonged unilateral convulsive seizure lasting more than 30 minutes
Development of persistent hemiplegia after seizure
Early onset of chronic focal epilepsy following hemiconvulsion
references: Nabbout R, Dulac O. Hemiconvulsion-hemiplegia-epilepsy syndrome. Epileptic Disord. 2008
Kramer U, et al. Hemiconvulsion-hemiplegia-epilepsy syndrome: clinical and imaging features. Neurology. 2005
